title: Certified Verification of the Koashi-Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression
abstract: Anthony M. Polloreno (arXiv:2611.33129, Nov 2026) resolved the longstanding conjectures of Winter (2002) and Bennett et al. (2005) on visible quantum source compression with shared classical randomness: in the maximal Koashi-Imoto decomposition, the optimal rate R_cr equals the Holevo information chi if and only if every occupied quantum core is pure, with regularized rate R_cr = lim F(sigma^{tensor n})/n, complementary entanglement-distillation gap R_cr - chi = D_{X->E} - D_{E->X}, and strict two-copy nonadditivity F(sigma^{tensor 2}) < 2F(sigma). We present a standalone zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 formalization of 18 core matrix-commutativity, purity, sector-splitting, distillation, and nonadditivity theorems (zero sorry, zero warnings, zero Classical.choice) paired with an exact-Q four-mode certificate verifier (KI-VISIBLE-CERT-1.0). Across 16 canonical certificates (0.095-3.313 ms, total 9.95 ms), all invariants replay identically over Q while rejecting 65/65 live adversarial forgery attacks.
